notes.title: Playtest Update 1
notes.content:
Here's some updates for the Fibula Playtest. Ive been focusing on improving game stability. Sometimes it runs amazing for 7 hours and uses 5 GB of RAM; other times it will crash after a minute. I've fixed some recent causes of that, upgraded Engine versions, and added the Unreal Engine crash reporter to the game build.

The other exciting feature is multiplayer session browser!! When starting a game you can enable multiplayer and enable "Public Session" to host a session publicly for others to join. There's no password protection step. Warning! Other players can open and loot your boxes and attack you. World PVP is enabled. I think there's lots of ways players could grief, so this is kind of an experiment in adversarial player behavior in the games current mechanics. Although take solace that NO inventory or experience is lost on death. This may change in the future, as an option. I never really intended to make a full loot MMO but we're not thattt far off but I want to see how many clients one PC can handle.

Changelog
[list]
[*] Horse Mounts. Each horse is 1 of 2 billion. Once tamed you can give them a name and they will join you on your adventure.
[*] Multiplayer Browser Support. Can host public lobbies. Play at your own risk. Selecting private multiplayer will allow Steam friends to invite and join.
[*] New Discord channel for #playtest-bugs
[*] Item Attributes 1.0
[*] Fixed Chat
[*] New F3 hotkey to show online player list.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes for April 15, 2025
notes.content:
Thank you everyone that's given the alpha playtest a go! It's been amazing to see the experiences players are having in the game, those intended and those not-so-intended but ultimately hilarious. With all the feedback so far, Ive gone ahead and pushed a game patch for some bug fixes, mechanics, and a note about controller support.

[h3]Changes[/h3]
[olist]
[*] The starting area monster spawns have been adjusted. The difficulty curve was a bit too strong ang meeting multiple new enemies in a short time was more overwhelming than fun for adventurers.
[*] First person animations for one handed combat has been adjusted to be more combo'able.
[*] Removed the stunning slash affect, it was a cool indicator for getting the upperhand in a fight, but had a distracting frequency.
[*] Minable nodes dont drop high quality metal anymore. Womp womp. Strategic resource is strategic.
[*] Skeletons got harder a slight overhaul. Their animations got an update and they resist being stunned so they get an opportunity to counter attack.
[*] Added audio cues for not having enough gold in trading and when skeletons aggro and attack
[*] No more Monk dialogue. He's just a trader until the upcoming NPC overhaul.
[/olist]

[h3]Bugs[/h3]
[olist]
[*] CONTROLLERS: players can look around and do basic combat controller now but outside a Steam Deck controller support is bad. I will be doing a technical dive into this.
[*] Bug fix: Fixed 2 pixel wide gap in between inventory slots that caused players to drop things instead of move them
[*] Fixed trying to split 1 item would create a phantom item locally but upon reload would recover accurate state.
[/olist]

notes.title: 🧙 Fibula Alpha Playtest is Live! 🛠️
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577045/56b42182c83e006d075edc2e6bf54427ff031d5c.png[/img]

Greetings, adventurers!

After many late nights, too much coffee, and countless iterations, I'm thrilled (and a bit nervous!) to announce the release of the Alpha Playtest for Fibula.

This is a huge milestone for the project, as it's the first time the game is out in the wild, and it marks the beginning of something I’ve imagined for a long time: [i]real[/i] community involvement. From here on out, you’re helping shape the future of this high fantasy action-adventure RPG.

[h3]🧩 What’s in the Alpha?[/h3]

This early build includes the foundational systems I’ve been working hard to bring to life. Here’s what you can expect to dig into:

[list]
[*] A skill-based progression system inspired by games like RuneScape and Skyrim
[*] A flexible class/race system with interchangeable combat styles
[*] Crafting, item quality upgrades, and early economic loops
[*] Over 100 diverse spells with a range of effects and use-cases, some useful others not so much
[*] A growing world filled with POIs, monsters, loot, and secrets
[*] Deployable objects that serve both progression and personalization
[*] Dangerous monsters, drop tables, basic inventory/equipment systems, and more
[/list]
This isn’t the final vision — just the starting point. But everything in this playtest is meant to give you a real feel for what Fibula is becoming.

[h3]🐞 What to Expect[/h3]

This is very much a work-in-progress, so you’ll definitely run into some bugs, placeholder content, and I imagine to be some weird pacing. But my goal with this version is to give you something that’s playable, understandable, and testable.

You might encounter including, but not limited to:
[list]
[*] Bugs (Please report them)
[*] Funky UI systems
[*] Wildly unbalanced mechanics
[*] Jank
[/list]
[h3]💬 Join the Community:[/h3]
Every bit of feedback helps — whether it’s a bug report, a comment about pacing, or even just letting me know what you liked or didn’t like. You can drop feedback in the [url=https://discord.gg/5BwM6Hj6qf]Discord Server[/url] or right here on Steam Discussions.

[h3]🧙 Why I’m Doing This[/h3]

Fibula is a passion project — something I’ve been slowly crafting out of my love for RPG systems, sprawling fantasy worlds, and games that offer some escapism to another world. I’m building this solo, but I know the only way it’s going to become something truly special is by opening it up and learning from the community.

So thank you, truly, for taking the time to try it out this early. I hope you find something exciting here, and I can’t wait to hear what you think.

See you out there, 
– Zizimaza
Side Quest Studios
